assumptions: Public competitor review text or CSV export with at least two reviews and at most 200,000 characters.
At most 200 reviews parsed and analyzed per execution.
Safe project context bounded to at most 8000 bytes from non-sensitive documentation (e.g. README, public docs).
cost_drivers: Bounded Codex procedure session using standard rate card; spending capped at configured sandbox ceiling.
Execution work scales with review corpus token count (up to 200 reviews) and output narrative size.
Zero paid external integrations or live provider API requests.
effects: Writes reports/COMPETITOR_REVIEW_MINER.md in the bound project workspace.
No external network egress, file mutations outside reports/COMPETITOR_REVIEW_MINER.md, secret access, or publication.

cases.description: Normal case: Three realistic competitor reviews with pain points, loved features, and a switching trigger.

inputs.reviews_text:
I switched away from AcmeDesk because pricing jumped 40% overnight for small teams.
AcmeDesk has a clean dashboard and great ticket triage, which our agents loved.
Sync is terribly slow and the mobile app crashes whenever resolving large queues.

cases.description: Boundary case: CSV with standard header column and reviews reaching processing bounds.

cases.description: Unusable result case: Single review line fails the two-review minimum, producing a diagnostic report.

rubric.question: Is every pain point, loved feature, and switching trigger backed by verbatim quotes from the supplied reviews?
Do the three growth opportunities offer concrete, testable positioning, copy, or roadmap actions rather than generic advice?
Does the workflow respect data bounds (cap at 200 reviews, safe file reads only, diagnostic output on invalid input) without hallucinations?
